about: A labelled question set for Ask the room's retrieval. One study group's material - lecture transcript lines, a summary, meeting documents and notes, with off-topic distractors - and questions whose answer is in a known passage. Many questions are paraphrases sharing no words with their answer, which is what keyword search misses; a few are exact identifiers (a command, a course code, a config value), which is what embeddings can blur. Used to choose the embedding model and to guard retrieval quality in tests. `followUps` are questions that only make sense after an earlier turn ("when is that due?"); each carries that turn as history.

passages.text: Welcome back. Today we're looking at how the gateway scales horizontally behind the load balancer, and why every replica has to be stateless.
Each replica keeps its websocket connections in memory, but anything shared, like which room a message goes to, lives in Redis pub/sub so every replica hears it.
When a job finishes, the worker writes an event to a Redis stream, and exactly one gateway picks it up through a consumer group.
If a worker dies halfway through, acks late means the job goes back on the queue and another worker takes it.
For the project we compared Kafka and Redis Streams. Kafka has better retention, but we would have to run ZooKeeper or KRaft, and nobody wants to operate that for a class project.
So the decision is Redis Streams, and we revisit it if we ever need replay beyond a few days.
Exactly-once delivery came up again. The honest answer is we get at-least-once plus idempotent handlers, which is what most real systems do.
Next week's reading is chapter four of Designing Data-Intensive Applications, the part on encoding and evolution.
The midterm is on the twelfth, it covers everything up to consensus, and it's open notes.

Key points

Stateless gateways behind a load balancer. Redis pub/sub for room fan-out. Redis Streams consumer groups for job events.

Action items

Priya writes the consumer groups section of the report by Friday. Marcus reruns the benchmark with three workers and posts the numbers.
Budget for the cloud credits is 50 dollars; we will turn the cluster off every night to stay under it.
Marcus measured a p95 latency of 180 milliseconds at 500 concurrent sockets on two replicas.

Open questions

Does the load balancer need sticky sessions for websockets? No - the upgrade pins the connection to one replica.

Glossary

Backpressure: slowing producers down when consumers can't keep up.
Photosynthesis lab write-up is due Monday for the biology group.
Office hours moved to Thursday at 3pm in room 204.
To recover messages a crashed consumer never acknowledged, run XAUTOCLAIM with a minimum idle time of thirty seconds.

Deadlines

CS-451 HW3 is due October 3. The CS-452 project proposal is due October 10.
Benchmark config: gateway replicas=2, worker concurrency=4, Redis maxmemory 512mb with allkeys-lru.
